::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

animals <- data.frame(species = c("cat", "dog", "cat"))
keep <- function(df, species) {
  filter(df, species == species)
}
keep(animals, species = "dog")
```
:::

## Why

In `filter()`, names are looked up first among the columns of the table, and only then in the function's environment. Both `species` therefore refer to the column, compared with itself: every row passes the filter.

The trap often shows up after the fact, when someone adds to the table a column that has the same name as an argument.

## The remedy

Say explicitly where each name comes from: `.data` for columns, `.env` for variables.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

keep <- function(df, species) {
  filter(df, .data$species == .env$species)
}
keep(animals, species = "dog")
```
:::
